summary: Created TagsManager in VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Library/ implementing all ITagsManager members.

EnsureLoadedAsync: SemaphoreSlim(1,1) + volatile bool + double-checked locking. LoadInternalAsync: 4 sequential queries (GetAllTagsAsync, GetAllCategoriesAsync, GetAllGrantsAsync, tags_movies count via IDbConnectionFactory).
ClampWeight: Math.Clamp to [TagConstants.MinWeight, TagConstants.MaxWeight].
BuildNameWithPath: iterative upward traversal of parent chain with visited guard against DB cycles.
RankImportance: quantile bucketing based on tags_movies count (top 10%→VeryHigh, +25%→High, +40%→Medium, remaining→Low, zero-use→Unused).
BuildClosure/ComputeTagClosure: BFS over unified parent + grant edges per tag.
GetEffectiveTagIds: union of precomputed closures for each stored tag ID.
WouldCreateParentCycle / WouldCreateGrantCycle: closure[oppositeEnd].Contains(proposedSource) or self-loop check.
DeleteCategoryAsync: throws InvalidOperationException for CategoryId 0 (Most Used virtual) and 1 (default). Delegates rest to repository.
All 16 mutation methods call repository, then ReloadAsync, then RaiseDataChanged.
MergeTagAsync: 7 SQL statements via direct IDbConnectionFactory (INSERT IGNORE SELECT + DELETE for movies/bookmarks/grants, UPDATE re-parent children, DELETE source).
GetDeleteImpactAsync / GetMergeImpactAsync: direct delegation to ITagsRepository.
Added AddSingleton<ITagsManager, TagsManager>() in Program.cs.
Build: 0 errors, 0 warnings. 228 unit tests pass.

comments.note: TagsManager.cs: Full reload (re-query all 4 SQL sources) is performed after every mutation including ConnectMovieTagAsync/DisconnectMovieTagAsync. This is simple and correct but inefficient for high-frequency tag-association operations (e.g., batch tagging). A future WP could optimise by doing incremental in-memory updates for association-only changes (which don't affect the graph closure or NameWithPath).

TagsManager.cs: MergeTagAsync issues 7+ SQL statements against a direct connection without a transaction. Partial failure (e.g. DB connection drops after books_bookmarks is rewired but before tags row is deleted) will leave an inconsistent state. Should be wrapped in a transaction.

TagsManager.cs: `_loadLock` SemaphoreSlim protects EnsureLoadedAsync/ReloadAsync but not direct reads of Tags/Categories from other threads. The reference assignments are atomic (reference types), so readers always see a consistent list snapshot, but there is no guarantee that Tags and Categories are updated atomically relative to each other. If strict atomicity is required, a single combined state record could be published as one reference swap.

TagsManager.cs: The quantile rank uses `(i < total * fraction)` with floating-point multiplication. For very large tag sets (>10k tags), floating-point rounding could misplace one boundary tag. Using integer ceiling thresholds would be more predictable.

summary: All 7 acceptance criteria verified and met.
AC1: volatile _isInitialized + SemaphoreSlim(1,1) + double-checked locking correctly prevents double-init under concurrency.
AC2: BuildClosure/ComputeTagClosure BFS traverses both parent chain (upward via ParentTagId) and outbound grant edges per tag. GetEffectiveTagIds unions per-tag closures for all stored IDs.
AC3: WouldCreateParentCycle checks _closure[proposedParentTagId].Contains(tagId); closure spans both parent+grant edges. WouldCreateGrantCycle is symmetric. Self-loop guard present for both.
AC4: DeleteCategoryAsync throws InvalidOperationException for categoryId==0 (Most Used virtual) and categoryId==1 (default).
AC5: ClampWeight uses Math.Clamp(tag.Weight, TagConstants.MinWeight=-10, TagConstants.MaxWeight=10). Applied as first step in LoadInternalAsync.

AC6: All 13 mutation methods (CreateTag, UpdateTag, DeleteTag, MergeTag, CreateCategory, UpdateCategory, DeleteCategory, AddGrant, RemoveGrant, ConnectMovieTag, DisconnectMovieTag, ConnectBookmarkTag, DisconnectBookmarkTag) call RaiseDataChanged() after successful completion.
AC7: Full solution build confirmed 0 errors, 0 warnings. Regression: 685 tests passed, 0 failed.

comments.note: TagsManager has no unit tests for its internal logic (BFS closure, cycle detection, weight clamping, concurrent init). A future WP should add unit tests using a fake ITagsRepository covering: (a) EnsureLoadedAsync is idempotent (called twice only loads once), (b) GetEffectiveTagIds returns parent-chain IDs, (c) WouldCreateParentCycle detects direct and transitive cycles, (d) ClampWeight clamps weights outside [-10, 10] range, (e) DataChanged fires exactly once per mutation.

TagsManager.WouldCreateParentCycle and WouldCreateGrantCycle read _closure without holding _loadLock. If called before EnsureLoadedAsync, _closure is empty and all cycle checks return false (no cycle detected). Callers must ensure EnsureLoadedAsync has completed before invoking cycle-guard methods; this is an expected usage contract but is not enforced by the API.

TagsManager.MergeTagAsync: 7 SQL statements via IDbConnectionFactory without a transaction — a partial failure leaves the DB in an inconsistent state (e.g., source tag rewired in tags_movies but not deleted from tags). Developer flagged this as high-priority debt. Should be wrapped in BeginTransactionAsync before M7 ships.

summary: PASS — TagsManager is a well-architected in-memory graph manager with clean separation of concerns.
EnsureLoadedAsync: volatile _isInitialized + SemaphoreSlim(1,1) + double-checked locking is the correct async thread-safe initialisation pattern.
LoadInternalAsync: 6-step pipeline (raw load → clamp weights → build lookup + grants adj → NameWithPath → rank importance → compute closure) is well-commented and logically ordered.

ComputeTagClosure BFS: correctly includes the starting tag, follows parent edges upward and outbound grant edges. Self-loop guard present. Verified against WouldCreateParentCycle / WouldCreateGrantCycle usage.
Mutation pattern is perfectly regular (repository call → ReloadAsync → RaiseDataChanged) across all 13 mutations — easy to reason about and maintain.
Applied Fix-Forward: PublishState() var threshold was assigned but never applied. Added explanatory comment + discard to clarify deferred filtering intent.

High-priority debt: MergeTagAsync (7 SQL statements without a transaction + SQL in manager layer bypassing ITagsRepository) must be addressed before M7 ships. Not a blocker for this WP's pipeline since the MergeTag feature isn't yet wired to any UI.

comments.note: TagsManager.PublishState(): var threshold was assigned from _settingsService.Current.Tagging.MostUsedThreshold but never referenced. Added a comment block explaining that threshold-based filtering is deferred to a future WP, plus a discard assignment (_ = threshold) to make the intent explicit. Non-behavioral. Build verified: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

TagsManager.MergeTagAsync issues 7 SQL statements via IDbConnectionFactory without a transaction. This is the highest-risk design issue in this WP — partial failure between any two steps (especially steps 3-5 involving tags_grants and tags row deletion) leaves the DB in an inconsistent state. Developer and QA both flagged this as high-priority debt. This must be addressed before M7 ships. A transaction wrapper (BeginTransactionAsync / CommitAsync / RollbackAsync via ADO.NET) is the correct remediation.

TagsManager.MergeTagAsync: SQL operations bypass ITagsRepository and use IDbConnectionFactory directly. This places SQL knowledge in the manager layer (a violation of the repository pattern). A better design would add MergeTagAsync to ITagsRepository, keeping all SQL in the Infrastructure/Library/DapperTagsRepository. The transaction wrapper WP should also migrate this SQL to the repository.
